sections.html:
Cole County splits tax duties between the Assessor, who puts a value on each parcel, and the Collector of Revenue, who mails statements and banks the payments. Find the Collector in Room 100 of the Courthouse Annex, 311 E High Street, Jefferson City 65101. The number is 573-634-9124, and staff answer weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. A drop box by the High Street entrance of the Annex is always accessible.

Hearing dates for the Board of Equalization come from the County Clerk. Above the county, the Missouri State Tax Commission oversees assessors and takes appeals once the local board has ruled. Take value complaints to the Assessor and billing problems to the Collector. A homeowner who walks into the wrong office usually gets pointed across the hall, so decide first whether your problem is the number or the bill. Your payment is divided among the state, municipalities, rural fire districts, the public library and the school districts.

You may pay a real estate bill from the day it reaches you, and the final date is December 31. Mailed checks count by postmark. Statements are mailed through November. Should yours be missing by the second week of December, the Collector wants a call, since a lost bill does not lift the tax or the late fees.

  • First-year delinquency can add as much as 25% in charges.
  • Tax sticks to the parcel, which means the next owner inherits any balance still open.
  • When a lender pays your tax from escrow, pass the bill along to the lender.
  • If a bill arrives for a house you have sold, send the Collector the new owner's name and address.

Online, cards carry a 2.25% convenience fee and e-checks a $1.75 fee, with 5 to 7 days for an e-check to clear. Other routes are the phone at 855-568-0066, dropping by the counter or mailing a check. A postmark of December 31 is timely, and the drop box stays open until midnight that night. Counter payments can be cash, personal check, cashier's check, bank draft, money order or card, and a single check can cover several bills.

sections.h2: How the amount is worked out
sections.html:
The math is assessed value divided by 100, then times the levy. Assessed value is only a slice of market value, and the size of the slice follows the parcel's class.

Class of real estateShare of value assessed
Residential19%
Agricultural12%
Commercial32%

Levies come from voters and the taxing districts, and the Assessor's site links a rate sheet. The county's real estate tax page walks through the method, and the Collector's staff will explain it by phone. If you want a rough bill for the house you are selling, first learn which taxing districts include the parcel, because the combined levy changes from place to place.

sections.h2: How to challenge a Cole County valuation
sections.html:
An informal chat with the Assessor is the first move. It is optional and offered on weekdays during office hours. Come with proof of market value, such as photographs, an inspection report, a recent appraisal or nearby sales. In the county's words, the Assessor's job is to keep values in step with the current market.

A formal review happens at the Board of Equalization, and the filing cutoff under RSMo 137.275 is the second Monday in July. Members include the County Commissioners, an Assessor who does not vote and appointees, with two city appointees added for parcels in Jefferson City. The County Clerk keeps the record and mails each taxpayer a written decision.

If you remain unhappy, take the matter to the State Tax Commission. RSMo 138.430 sets the appeal period at the one stated in that chapter or 30 days after the local board finishes, whichever ends later. Those sessions are usually in September and October with a single Administrative Hearing Officer. An appraisal is expected, and hiring a lawyer is up to you.

After three delinquent years, a parcel qualifies for the county's certificate sale. The auction opens at 10 in the morning at the Cole County Courthouse, and RSMo 140.150 places it on the fourth Monday in August statewide. Pay the Collector the tax, penalty, interest and costs ahead of time and the parcel comes out of the sale.

  • The Jefferson City News Tribune publishes the parcel list three weeks running before the sale.
  • A winning bid earns a certificate of purchase, and the original owner can redeem for a year after the sale.
  • Existing liens outlast both the sale and the redemption period.
  • A bidder who wins and then fails to pay faces a 25% penalty and a prosecuting attorney fee.

A seller who is behind can ask the Collector for a current payoff. Nothing is paid to that office at the sale itself, so get any payoff amount in writing by way of the title company.

sections.h2: Who pays when a house changes hands
sections.html:
Ownership in the fall decides who pays the November bill, so after a mid-year sale the buyer does. Closing normally prorates the tax and gives the buyer a credit for the days or months the seller owned the place. The buyer pays the full bill by December 31.

Central Missouri holds Cole County, just south of the Missouri River, and Jefferson City is both the seat and the state capital. The July 1, 2025 estimates list 77,908 people and 33,956 housing units. Owners occupy 67.9% of units, the 2020 to 2024 median value is $229,600, and median household income is $74,876. Median rent is $834, and 154 building permits were issued in 2025.

A tidy way to prepare: ask the Collector for your parcel balance, and check the taxing districts shown on your last statement. The title company can then print the tax line for your settlement statement, and the Collector only needs the new owner's mailing address once the sale is done. Cash Home Buyers can purchase a house with back taxes or a lien problem, with the closing agent clearing the balance out of the price, so nothing is left to chase afterward.

Pull together a short folder before the listing goes live: your latest statement, the Collector's payoff figure, any Assessor notice showing the value, and notes from any informal talk with the Assessor. Buyers' agents often ask what the tax will be, and a folder like this lets you answer from paper instead of memory.

If you escrow, tell your lender about the sale so it can send any leftover cushion your way. Keep the closing statement with your records, along with a copy of the paid receipt, in case a question about the year's tax comes up months later.

faqs.q: When does Cole County property tax become late?
faqs.a: Right after December 31. You can pay any time after the bill arrives, mail counts by postmark, and the courthouse drop box is good until midnight on the last day. A first delinquent year can add up to 25% in charges.

faqs.q: Will the Collector mail me a bill?
faqs.a: Yes, during November. Nothing by the second week of December? Phone 573-634-9124. A lost bill changes nothing about what you owe or the late fees.

faqs.q: What is the last day to appeal to the Board of Equalization?
faqs.a: The second Monday in July, with the filing made through the County Clerk. A talk with the Assessor can come before that.

faqs.q: Who owes the tax after a mid-year sale?
faqs.a: The buyer is billed for the full amount in December and normally gets a proration credit at closing. The Collector receives nothing at the table. If the bill still comes to you, mail the Collector the buyer's address.

faqs.q: How many years of unpaid tax lead to a sale?
faqs.a: Three years. Then the parcel may be offered at the August certificate sale, though the owner can still pay beforehand or redeem during the year that follows.
